newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold seen under pressure.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold seen under pressure.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30

Further investment fund selling out of New York on Wednesday is likely to pressure gold lower during European trading on Thursday, and several traders and analysts said prices might test $320.00 an ounce support.
Silver was likely to be pressured by gold, while platinum was seen holding steady at lower levels as traders digested news that Russia planned to send shipments to Japan by Monday.
GOLD - Investment fund selling amid downtrending chart signals and recent strength in the U.S. dollar and equity markets is likely to pressure gold lower.
Traders and chartists said they would not be surprised if gold tests and possibly breaks below $320.00 an ounce by the end of this week.

Analysts said the depth and duration of this week's retreat warns of further near-term weakness. "There is little to hold gold above $320.00 at the moment, expect further weakness," one trader commented.
The break below $322.00 overnight does not bode well for the market, the trader added.

"The market has been heading lower all week, though we expected support at $322.00," he said. Below $320.00 there is some support available between $318.50 and $319.50 but several traders believe the inability of gold to bounce significantly this week targets levels towards $315.00 near term.
Resistance was pegged at $325.00.
At 0805 GMT spot gold was indicated at $320.80/$321.20, versus Wednesday's London close of $324.50/$325.00.
SILVER - Seen under pressure in line with gold, but conditions were likely to remain fairly thin as operators attention focused on the gold market.
Support was pegged at $4.17, followed by $4.00.
Resistance was seen at $4.40/$4.45, followed $4.60.
At 0815 GMT spot silver was indicated at $4.28/$4.30, versus $4.31/$4.33.
PLATINUM - Dipped early on news that Russia plans to send platinum to Japan for arrival by Monday.
Traders said they did not expect prices to come under strong downside pressure as the physical market remained tight.
At 0820 platinum was indicated at $414.00/$415.00, against $416.00/$419.00.
